title: Sauce de woulahada (Zom Leaf Sauce with Smoked Fish)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Fresh woulahada (zom) leaves boiled 10 minutes in natron water to keep them green, added to a fried smoked-fish base with peanut paste, and simmered 15–20 minutes.
longDesc: p. 60 of the October 2023 recipe book. The method follows the foleré sauce (CMR059), with fresh woulahada (zom) leaves boiled 10 minutes in water with natron — the book says natron keeps the sauce green — then added to the fried onion, smoked-fish, tomato and spice base with roasted peanut paste, and simmered 15–20 minutes. No quantities are printed. ‘Zom’ is also the nightshade leaf in the Afrik sanga page; the book calls it woulahada (zom) and neither page states its botanical identity.
ingredients: Fresh woulahada (zom) leaves — quantity not printed
Roasted peanut paste — quantity not printed
Water, oil, onion, garlic, tomatoes, bell pepper, leek, parsley, celery, white pepper, ginger, salt, chilli — quantities not printed
steps: Boil the leaves 10 minutes in water with natron. Drain.
Fry the onion. Add the fish, tomatoes, garlic, green condiments and spices and simmer.
Add water, the peanut paste and salt.
chefTips: The printed reason for the natron is to keep the sauce green.
No other doneness cue is printed.
commonMistakes: Skipping the natron and losing the colour.
Assuming the botanical identity of zom.
healthBenefits: A leafy green sauce with smoked fish and peanuts.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Sauce de woulahada (zom) au poisson fumé’ (p. 60).
